categories.label: User Library Caches
categories.notes: Safe regenerable app caches. Prefer contents-only delete with min_age. Exclude CloudKit, HomeKit, Find My, and Safari from bulk wipe (Safari handled separately). Do not delete the Caches directory itself.

categories.label: User Library Logs
categories.notes: User-space app logs only (~/Library/Logs). Safe to remove contents; leave the Logs folder. Do not include /var/log or /private/var/log (system).

categories.label: Saved Application State
categories.notes: Window restore / Resume state (*.savedState). Apps recreate on next launch. Only clears restore data, not documents.

categories.label: User temporary directory (TMPDIR)
categories.notes: Resolves to this user's /private/var/folders/.../T/. Clean aged contents only; skip open/in-use files. Never wipe sibling user folders under /private/var/folders.

categories.label: Shared system temp (/tmp)
categories.notes: World-writable shared temps. Default off: other users and running processes may use files here. Age-filter + contents-only if enabled; never delete the directory nodes.

categories.label: Darwin /private/var/folders (report-only)
categories.notes: Per-user 0/C/T trees for all accounts. Report size only; never auto-delete the tree. User cleanup goes through $TMPDIR (T) or careful owned C caches, not a bulk rm of /private/var/folders.

categories.label: Homebrew download cache
categories.notes: Default brew --cache is $HOME/Library/Caches/Homebrew (overridable via HOMEBREW_CACHE). Cached bottles/sources; brew re-downloads as needed. Prefer brew cleanup when available.

categories.label: Xcode DerivedData
categories.notes: Default DerivedData location (Xcode Settings > Locations). Safe but forces full rebuilds/reindex. Default off for developer machines.

categories.label: Xcode device support symbols
categories.notes: Symbols for attached devices; large and regenerable when the device reconnects. Prefer deleting old OS version folders only.

categories.label: Xcode Archives (report-only)
categories.notes: May be required for App Store uploads, TestFlight, and crash symbolication (dSYM). Measure only; delete only via Organizer with user intent.

categories.label: CoreSimulator caches
categories.notes: Simulator dyld/runtime caches only. Do not delete Devices or system runtimes under /Library/Developer/CoreSimulator without explicit user action (use simctl for devices/runtimes).

categories.label: Mail Downloads (attachments)
categories.notes: Attachments Mail opened and copied here; not mailbox store. Can free space but may remove local copies still wanted. Never touch $HOME/Library/Mail or other Mail container data (Accounts, MailData, Preferences).

categories.label: Browser disk caches
categories.notes: Disk/network caches only; do not touch Application Support profiles, cookies, logins, or ~/Library/Safari bookmarks/history. Close browsers first when possible. Safari/WebKit caches can be recreated but are stickier while Safari is running.

categories.label: Quick Look thumbnail cache
categories.notes: Thumbnail caches rebuilt by Quick Look as files are previewed.

categories.label: Swift Package Manager cache
categories.notes: Resolved SPM package cache; re-downloaded on next build. Default off to avoid surprise network/build cost on CI-like machines.

categories.label: User Library Caches
categories.notes: Primary safe reclaim surface. Delete contents of aged app cache dirs, not the Caches folder node itself. Exclude CloudKit, HomeKit, Find My, and full Safari tree from bulk auto-clean unless browser-cache category is on. Never scan /System/Library/Caches or /Library/Caches as rule roots.

categories.label: User Library Logs
categories.notes: User-scoped app logs only. Regenerable diagnostic text; keep min_age (e.g. 7d). Do not touch /var/log or /Library/Logs without elevated opt-in.

categories.label: Saved Application State
categories.notes: Window restoration blobs; apps recreate on next launch. Low user impact.

categories.label: User temporary directory
categories.notes: macOS per-user temp is typically under /var/folders/.../T via $TMPDIR. Only delete aged contents; never target /private/var/folders wholesale or other users' folders.

categories.label: Homebrew download cache
categories.notes: Default brew --cache location. Bottles/sources re-download; prefer brew cleanup for live Cellar interaction. Safe contents wipe of aged downloads.

categories.label: Quick Look thumbnail cache
categories.notes: Thumbnail indexes rebuild via qlmanage/Finder. Narrow paths only; do not wipe all CloudKit.

categories.label: User Trash
categories.notes: User-intended discard but irreversible after empty. Off by default; confirm UI/dry-run. Volume Trashes under /.Trashes are out of scope for auto-clean.

categories.label: Xcode DerivedData
categories.notes: Build intermediates; next build is cold/full. Safe to clear when Xcode is quit. Not source code.

categories.label: Xcode iOS DeviceSupport
categories.notes: Device symbols for debugging; large and regenerable when device reconnects. Keep recent platforms if actively debugging.

categories.label: CoreSimulator caches
categories.notes: dyld and related simulator caches grow large and rebuild. Do NOT auto-delete Devices/ (wipes simulator VMs and app data); that stays report-only or manual simctl.

categories.label: Xcode Archives
categories.notes: May hold dSYMs and App Store submission artifacts. Measure and list only; never auto-delete.

categories.label: Browser disk cache (not profiles)
categories.notes: HTTP/disk caches only. Leaves cookies, passwords, extensions, Local Storage, and profile DBs alone. Default off because active browsers lock files and Safari cache layout varies by version.

categories.label: Browser profiles and privacy data
categories.notes: EXPLICIT PRIVACY MODE ONLY. Logs users out, drops history/cookies/site data. Blocked by never_touch for normal auto-clean; enable only with dual confirmation and dry-run. Prefer browser-native clear APIs when available.

categories.label: Mail attachment downloads
categories.notes: Attachments Mail saved to disk; may be the only local copy. Requires narrow allowlist of this subpath only; never delete $HOME/Library/Mail or the whole com.apple.mail container.

categories.label: Local iPhone/iPad backups
categories.notes: Full device backups via Finder/iTunes. Irreplaceable without another backup. Report size only; user deletes via Finder Manage Backups or explicit manual action.

categories.label: Language package manager caches
categories.notes: Regenerable download caches for common toolchains on macOS. Do not delete pnpm global store, full .cargo registry sources blindly, or project node_modules/target dirs from this category.

categories.label: XDG user cache
categories.notes: Non-essential app caches per XDG (default $HOME/.cache). Prefer contents-only delete with min_age_days>=3. Exclude GPU/driver shader dirs (mesa_shader_cache, nvidia, amd/gl_shader_cache) if wipe causes long recompiles. Do not treat as a free-for-all over nested browser profile data if linked outside pure cache trees.

categories.label: Thumbnail cache
categories.notes: FreeDesktop thumbnail cache (normal/large/x-large/xx-large/fail). Regenerated by file managers. Legacy ~/.thumbnails still appears on older desktops. Safe contents wipe; min_age_days>=7 optional to keep recent previews.

categories.label: User temp and Trash
categories.notes: Age-filter $TMPDIR (min_age_days>=2). Trash is user-recoverable junk. Never wipe whole $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR (sockets/locks for live session); if included, only age-stale nested cache-like subdirs or omit runtime entirely and keep Trash+$TMPDIR. Prefer omitting $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR from auto-clean in implementation.

categories.label: User log files
categories.notes: Restrict to **/*.log and **/*.old under state trees. XDG_STATE_HOME defaults to $HOME/.local/state. Do not delete non-log state (history DBs, app state). min_age_days>=14.

categories.label: systemd journal (journald)
categories.notes: Persistent journals live under /var/log/journal/<machine-id>/; volatile under /run/log/journal. Never unlink active *.journal files from disk directly. Size control must be journalctl --vacuum-size/--vacuum-time (optionally after --rotate). Report size only; cleaning requires a dedicated privileged vacuum action, not generic file delete.

categories.label: APT package cache (Debian/Ubuntu)
categories.notes: Downloaded .deb payloads; equivalent to apt clean. Regenerable; needs root. Keep lock files; do not delete /var/lib/apt/lists (package indexes) or /var/lib/dpkg. default_enabled false because system/root scope.

categories.label: pacman package cache (Arch family)
categories.notes: Default CacheDir is /var/cache/pacman/pkg/. Safe to remove packages but loses easy downgrade/reinstall offline. Prefer paccache -rkN semantics over wiping every package. Needs root. Never touch /var/lib/pacman.

categories.label: DNF package cache (Fedora/RHEL)
categories.notes: dnf4 uses /var/cache/dnf; Fedora 41+ dnf5 also uses /var/cache/libdnf5. Metadata and any keepcache RPMs are regenerable (dnf clean all). Needs root. Never delete /var/lib/dnf or RPM DB under /var/lib/rpm.

categories.label: systemd-tmpfiles temporary dirs
categories.notes: systemd-tmpfiles ages /tmp (~10d) and /var/tmp (~30d) via tmpfiles.d. Auto-clean only aged file contents, never the directory roots, never sockets currently in use, never /tmp/.X11-unix, /tmp/.ICE-unix, systemd private dirs. Never delete tmpfiles configs under /etc/tmpfiles.d, /usr/lib/tmpfiles.d, /run/tmpfiles.d, or $HOME/.config/user-tmpfiles.d. Prefer invoking systemd-tmpfiles --clean when possible.

categories.label: Flatpak per-app caches
categories.notes: Sandbox XDG cache for each Flatpak app under ~/.var/app/<app-id>/cache. Regenerable. Do not delete sibling config or data dirs. min_age_days>=3.

categories.label: Flatpak installs and unused runtimes
categories.notes: Installed apps/runtimes live in user ~/.local/share/flatpak and system /var/lib/flatpak; leftover app data after uninstall stays in ~/.var/app/<id>. Blind rm breaks installs and OSTree repos. Report sizes only; cleanup via flatpak uninstall --unused [--delete-data] and flatpak repair, not file-level delete of repo/objects.

categories.label: Snap download cache
categories.notes: snapd working/download cache; safe to clear (may force re-download). Needs root. Distinct from mounted/active snap images in /var/lib/snapd/snaps.

categories.label: Snap revisions and user leftovers
categories.notes: Old revisions under /var/lib/snapd/snaps and ~/snap/<name>/<rev> must be pruned with snap remove --revision or snap set system refresh.retain=N, not rm. User data in ~/snap and /var/snap can hold important app state. Report only; optional future medium rule limited to $HOME/snap/*/*/.cache if clearly cache.

categories.label: Old kernels and modules
categories.notes: Always report-only. Removing the running or only fallback kernel bricks the system. Instruct users to purge via apt autoremove / dnf remove $(dnf repoquery --installonly --latest-limit=-2 -q) / package-manager tools. Never auto-delete /boot or module trees.

categories.label: User TEMP
categories.notes: Default user temp is %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp (via %TEMP%/%TMP%). Delete contents only; keep the folder; skip in-use files; min_age_days >= 1–2 recommended.

categories.label: System TEMP
categories.notes: C:\Windows\Temp (or %WINDIR%\Temp). Often needs elevation; many files locked by services. Contents-only; never delete the Temp directory itself.

categories.label: Prefetch
categories.notes: Default %WINDIR%\Prefetch (*.pf, ReadyBoot). Safe-ish contents clear but slows cold starts until rebuilt and erases launch traces. Prefer report or opt-in; do not wipe Layout.ini aggressively; avoid if Superfetch/SysMain analysis matters.

categories.label: WinSxS component store
categories.notes: Report size only. Never auto-delete. Cleanup only via DISM StartComponentCleanup / Storage Sense / Disk Cleanup. Manual deletes break servicing.

categories.label: Delivery Optimization cache
categories.notes: Default cache drive is %SystemDrive% (DOModifyCacheDrive). Live cache usually under NetworkService DeliveryOptimization\Cache; alternate layouts exist. Prefer Settings/Disk Cleanup; stop DoSvc if clearing files; admin required; cache rebuilds on next updates.

categories.label: Browser disk caches
categories.notes: Cache-only under Chromium profiles and Firefox cache2/startupCache; INetCache is legacy web cache. Never touch Cookies, Login Data, Web Data, Local Storage, IndexedDB, Preferences, or whole User Data/profile roots. Close browsers first.

categories.label: Windows.old
categories.notes: Previous Windows installation after in-place upgrade. Report only; remove via Settings > System > Storage or Disk Cleanup (Previous Windows installation). Direct delete may fail ACLs and blocks rollback.

categories.label: Recycle Bin
categories.notes: Per-volume $Recycle.Bin holds recoverable user files. Opt-in only. Path expander must treat $Recycle.Bin as a literal name (not a $variable). Prefer SHEmptyRecycleBin API over raw deletes when possible.

categories.label: Thumbnail and icon cache
categories.notes: thumbcache_*.db under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Explorer; legacy Thumbs.db in folders. Safe to delete; Explorer rebuilds. May need Explorer restart if files are locked. Do not wipe entire Explorer folder (other settings live there).

categories.label: Node.js project node_modules
categories.notes: Regenerable via npm/yarn/pnpm install. Never full-home auto-delete: only under explicit project scan roots, require package.json/lockfile sibling, min_age_days>=14, max_depth bound. Excludes Yarn PnP .yarn/cache (project policy) and pnpm content store.

categories.label: Rust Cargo target/ build dirs
categories.notes: Default is workspace-root target/ (or CARGO_TARGET_DIR). Match only when Cargo.toml exists at parent/workspace root. Forces full recompile. Do not delete $HOME/.cargo/bin or source crates.

categories.label: Web/frontend build outputs (dist, .next, out)
categories.notes: Common regenerable frontend outputs. Avoid bare **/build (collides with CMake/Python/Make). Require project markers (package.json, etc.) and min_age. May contain deliberately kept release artifacts: keep opt-in.

categories.label: Python __pycache__ and .pyc
categories.notes: Bytecode is always regenerable. Default-enabled only under known cache trees (existing dev-pycache-home pattern). Project-tree **/__pycache__ should stay opt-in or age-gated to avoid walking all of $HOME.

categories.label: npm and Yarn download caches
categories.notes: Official npm cache: ~/.npm (posix) or %LocalAppData%/npm-cache (Windows). Yarn classic/berry user cache under XDG or Library/Caches. Prefer contents delete + min_age_days>=14. Not node_modules, not pnpm store.

categories.label: pip and Python package caches
categories.notes: HTTP wheel/sdist cache only. Do not touch virtualenvs (.venv, venv) or conda envs.

categories.label: Gradle dependency and build caches
categories.notes: Gradle User Home caches (~/.gradle/caches). Safe to wipe but forces large re-downloads. Never delete project source or required wrapper scripts outside dists. Project-level .gradle/ is separate and higher risk.

categories.label: Xcode DerivedData and iOS DeviceSupport
categories.notes: DerivedData default remains ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData. Regenerable; full rebuilds. Archives (~/Library/Developer/Xcode/Archives) stay report-only (dSYM/App Store).

categories.label: Android SDK caches and unused system-images
categories.notes: SDK defaults: macOS ~/Library/Android/sdk, Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\Android\Sdk, Linux ~/Android/Sdk or ANDROID_HOME. Only caches/temp/system-images leftovers—never whole SDK, platform-tools, or licenses. AVD userdata is never_touch.

categories.label: Docker Desktop images, volumes, and VM disk
categories.notes: macOS Docker.raw under Containers/.../vms/0/data; Windows docker_data.vhdx under Local\Docker\wsl (path varies by Desktop version). File-delete destroys all images/volumes. Report size only; reclaim via docker system prune / Desktop.

categories.label: asdf/mise download and install caches
categories.notes: Download/cache only (asdf downloads/; mise cache dir). Does not remove installed tool versions. Prefer contents delete + min_age_days>=7.

categories.label: asdf/mise installed tool versions (unused)
categories.notes: asdf: ${ASDF_DATA_DIR:-$HOME/.asdf}/installs/<plugin>/<version>. mise: ~/.local/share/mise/installs (XDG). Never bulk-delete: only report, or delete versions proven unused vs .tool-versions/mise.toml/global config. Keep shims/plugins/config.

categories.label: pnpm content-addressable store
categories.notes: Shared store; deleting breaks projects until re-fetch. Prefer pnpm store prune for unused packages. Report size only unless user explicitly overrides.

categories.label: Cargo registry and git dependency cache
categories.notes: Downloaded crate sources/cache only—not project target/. Never delete $HOME/.cargo/bin (installed binaries) or .cargo/config.toml.

categories.label: macOS recent documents and apps
categories.notes: Opt-in privacy wipe of Apple menu / Finder recents. Confirmed .sfl4 on current macOS; globs cover older .sfl2/.sfl3. Does not include FavoriteItems/FavoriteVolumes/ProjectsItems. Regenerates as files are opened.

categories.label: Per-app Open Recent and Office recents
categories.notes: ApplicationRecentDocuments holds per-app .sfl* Open Recent lists. Office securebookmarks.plist files hold Word/Excel/PowerPoint recent lists on Mac. Close Office first. Cloud-synced Microsoft account recents may reappear after sign-in.

categories.label: Clipboard history stores (third-party)
categories.notes: No durable system clipboard history path on macOS comparable to Windows Clipboard folder; targets common managers (Maccy, Paste, Alfred). May hold passwords and tokens. Quit the manager before delete. Prefer contents of store dirs, not unrelated container siblings.

categories.label: Shell and REPL history
categories.notes: NEVER default-enable. Histories can contain secrets, tokens, and private paths. Does not touch shell config (.zshrc, .bashrc, fish config). New empty history files may be recreated on next session.

categories.label: Browser cookies (opt-in)
categories.notes: Opt-in only. Logs out websites. Safari primary store is the sandboxed Cookies.binarycookies path; legacy Library/Cookies may still exist. Chrome/Firefox profile DBs only; never Login Data, Web Data, or full profile dirs. Close browsers first.

categories.label: Browser localStorage and site storage (opt-in)
categories.notes: Opt-in only. Clears origin-scoped site data (sessions, offline apps). Safari WebsiteData/Default also holds IndexedDB and service workers under origin subdirs. Keep separate from browser disk cache rules. Close browsers first.
